content.intro: Learn redirects and not-found responses through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Redirects and Not-Found Responses matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines redirects and not-found responses as part of django architecture and http fundamentals. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: Redirecting between URLs; Named redirects; Temporary and permanent redirects; Raising or returning a 404 response; Custom 404 and 500 error pages. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: Redirecting between URLs
items.text: Redirecting between URLs is part of the request/response contract. Match routes and methods explicitly, return an appropriate response/status, and test success, missing-resource and unauthorized paths.

items.title: Named redirects
items.text: Redirect by a named route or a validated destination. Never build an open redirect from an untrusted query parameter; distinguish temporary from permanent redirects.

items.title: Temporary and permanent redirects
items.text: Redirect by a named route or a validated destination. Never build an open redirect from an untrusted query parameter; distinguish temporary from permanent redirects.

items.title: Raising or returning a 404 response
items.text: Raising or returning a 404 response is part of the request/response contract. Match routes and methods explicitly, return an appropriate response/status, and test success, missing-resource and unauthorized paths.

items.title: Custom 404 and 500 error pages
items.text: Treat Custom 404 and 500 error pages as a reproducible diagnostic: capture the exact input and observed result, isolate one hypothesis, and add a regression test once the cause is fixed. Avoid exposing internal stack traces or secrets to public users.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: Redirects and Not-Found Responses
content_blocks.code:
from django.urls import path
from . import views

urlpatterns = [
    path("items/<int:item_id>/", views.item_detail, name="item-detail"),
]
content_blocks.expected_output: The route converter passes an integer item_id to the named view.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Open a local project using the documented Django 6.1-compatible Python environment. If this snippet depends on model names, URL configuration, settings, or an optional package, add those prerequisites before running it. Otherwise inspect it as a static example. CodeLeaf browser preview does not execute Django/Python server code.
content_blocks.troubleshooting: The view and project include() wiring must exist; URL conversion does not perform authorization or database lookup.

content_blocks.title: Guided walkthrough
content_blocks.text: First identify the input and the responsible Django component. Next trace how the example moves through “Redirects and Not-Found Responses” and the related concept “Redirecting between URLs”. Predict the result before running or inspecting it. Finally compare the observed behavior with the expected result and the cited official documentation.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Change one input or configuration choice related to Redirecting between URLs. Write down the expected outcome, test one normal case and one invalid or boundary case, then record what changed. Do not add real credentials or sensitive production data.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Common pitfalls include skipping a required configuration/import, copying a fragment without its model or URL context, trusting client input, or treating a development-only behavior as production-ready. Check the earliest failing assumption, consult the version-specific docs, and add a regression test for the failure you found.

content_blocks.title: Recap
